title: Why New Jersey needs stricter snow removal rules for drivers - NewsBreak
text:
By Mike Brant ,
6 hours ago Canva (Townsquare Illustration) Normally I‚Äôm not a fan of the phrase ticket blitz since it gives off negative vibes toward police officers. However, what might appear to be a ticket blitz during and after our historic blizzard is 100% necessary.
Now to be clear,¬†there is no actual call for this. Rather, I‚Äôm making the argument that every town in New Jersey should do this, but toward specific drivers only.
And I‚Äôll make this very simple. If you‚Äôre someone who‚Äôs driving around and still haven‚Äôt cleaned the mountain of snow off the roof of your vehicle, then you absolutely deserve a ticket. Period. Hard stop.
And that‚Äôs exactly why I would be in favor of a ticket blitz if the state decided to have one. A blitz on those specific drivers who just won‚Äôt clean off their vehicles.
ALSO READ: Does NJ really only allow 24-hours to clear snow from vehicles? However, there‚Äôs another component to this that isn‚Äôt about what happens after the storm. There‚Äôs also those drivers who deserve tickets for what they do during the storm.
More tickets for parking We were on the air all throughout New Jersey‚Äôs historic blizzard. I myself was on both the morning of Feb. 22, and the early morning overnight hours on Feb. 23, during the brunt of the storm.
I was getting a lot of calls from plow drivers that all had one common complaint. Far too many people kept their vehicles parked on the main streets despite being ordered to move them. This, in turn, made it that much more difficult for plow drivers to do their jobs.
I did, however, find out that cops were issuing tickets for those vehicles, and I‚Äôm glad they did. One person who called in actually complained he got a ticket for doing just this and bashed the police to no end.
But you know what? The police were right to do that, and you were wrong for keeping your vehicle in the way of the plows. Plus, you forced the police to issue tickets during a blizzard, something I‚Äôm sure they didn‚Äôt want to do.
Please blitz the next storm To all the police officers and plow drivers that had to work during the blizzard, thank you for all you do. For those who wouldn‚Äôt move their cars out of the way during the storm, too bad. Go to court and pay the fine.
And for those who leave the snow on the roofs afterward? Oh well. It‚Äôs dangerous to do that and that snow and ice can seriously injure someone else or cause an accident should it fly off. Go to court and answer to the judge. (Read about what towns have been issuing tickets here ).

Gallery Credit: Kylie Moore Kylie Moore Wear your pajamas inside out I definitely remember doing this in elementary school.
Did it always work? No.
Did it sometimes lead to a snow day? Yep, and that was good enough for 8-year-old me! Kylie Moore Place a white crayon on your window overnight It‚Äôs as if you‚Äôre sending a message to the outside: I want you to be snowy white when I wake up. Kylie Moore Yell ‚ÄúSNOW DAY‚Äù into the freezer Hey, if you‚Äôre going to yell your affirmations anywhere it may as well be the place that‚Äôs already freezing. Kylie Moore Flush ice cubes down the toilet Parents might not love this one, but they gotta understand that desperate times call for desperate measures. Kylie Moore Put a spoon under your pillow This one I can‚Äôt find the logic in, but I‚Äôm not going to stop anyone from doing it.
If taking the spoon out of the silverware drawer gives you the snow day you deserve, I say ‚Äúgo for it.‚Äù Kylie Moore Brush your teeth with your non-dominant hand Your guess is as good as mine on this one. Kylie Moore Eat a bunch of ice cream Don‚Äôt tempt me with a good time, I‚Äôll do this task snow day or not. Just no hot fudge because the heat could melt the snow! The above post reflects the thoughts and observations of New Jersey 101.5 weekend host & content contributor Mike Brant . Any opinions expressed are his own.
